title: Airframe & Structure
details: FDM-printed PETG or nylon for early hull and frame iterations for fast turnaround; migration to CNC-cut carbon fiber sheet or wound-tube frame once geometry is locked, for flight-weight parts with long fatigue life.

title: Dual-Mode Propulsion
details: Dual-path gearbox concept — 12.7:1 reduction on the underwater path, direct drive on the aerial path, selected by motor direction, so the propeller never reverses.
Waterproof brushless motors (marine-rated 2307.5-class). Blue Robotics T200 flooded-brushless thrusters as a COTS benchmark and sourced-thruster fallback.

Thrust vectoring under evaluation as an alternative to differential thrust in water mode. The air/water drive interface is identified as the most failure-prone mechanical joint on this class of vehicle.

title: Flight & Dive Control
summary: A shared controller across both media.
details: Pixhawk-class controller (Cube Orange or Pixhawk 6X) running PX4. Cascaded PID — attitude to rate to motor mixer — as the baseline before any learned control.
PX4’s uuv_pos_control and uuv_att_control modules only cover multirotor underwater control, so a tail-sitter requires a custom airframe definition plus a hand-written mode-switch controller.
ArduSub retained as a fallback for depth-hold logic.

title: Onboard Compute & Autonomy
details: AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 (Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC with built-in DPU), targeting sub-20 ms onboard vision inference under 10 W.
NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano as a backup path so autonomy work is never blocked on FPGA toolchain bring-up. ROS 2 for the sensor and autonomy pipeline, bridged via MAVROS or px4_ros_com.

title: Waterproofing & Sealing
summary: A watertight core, designed for iteration.
details: UV-cure conformal coating on all boards (roughly 15 minute cure versus about 24 hours for silicone, which matters at iteration speed). Fully potted ESCs.
IP67/IP68 target for the flight controller and compute enclosure. Marine-grade wet-mate connectors at every water-crossing seam.

title: Communications
details: Published depth limits set the constraint: roughly 1.5 m for a 900 MHz RC link and roughly 2 m for 433 MHz telemetry — both effectively near-surface only.
Mission design therefore assumes periodic surfacing for RF check-in. A low-bandwidth acoustic modem is held as an option if sustained deep operation becomes a requirement.

title: Simulation & Validation
details: SolidWorks for CAD and per-sub-assembly mass properties → Simscape Multibody for rigid-body dynamics → Simulink for control design → SolidWorks Flow Simulation for fast early aero sweeps → OpenFOAM interFoam (Volume-of-Fluid) or ANSYS Fluent for the water-entry/exit transient → PX4 SITL + Gazebo for full-vehicle SITL → hardware-in-the-loop with a real Pixhawk → bench test of the propulsion mechanism → pool test → open water.
